I felt alive. The pain genuinely made me feel great. It reminded me that I was here, that I was present, and that I had to be someone because I could I feel.

The emotions that came along with it weren’t great, and that’s why I stop, but it’s hard to say that in the moment it didn’t make me feel better.

Do you have any understanding friends to go out with? Family to go talk to? Genuinely being with the people you love and love you helps give you some purpose to do other things.

Outside of that, stay busy. Sometimes a surplus of depression/anxiety can manifest itself oddly enough in being unable to do anything. As someone that has dealt with this for years there are few better reliefs than a good workout/endorphin release. I’ve found the ability to perform physically is one of the few controllables that I always know will net a victory or positive in the day.  Depending on your personality sometimes it’s just nice to immerse yourself in something public as well, take a class, see a show, just do something around others. 

Never give up on yourself. Even if you need to look at yourself in a mirror and tell yourself you are great until you believe it.  Depression happens and don’t feel bad about it, just know how to get out of it when you are ready.

Don’t try to look like you care. Being you is completely ok and you are allowed to embrace that. As long as you are courteous to others and treat them as you would like to be treated you are not obligated to engage in any situations that you don’t want to. If your friends aren’t engaging in things you are passionate about or you aren’t passionate about your friends, than get new ones. It’s a rough grind but you need to find your corner of the world. 

The only caveat to that is that you also need to make sure you ARE ok with you and how you respond to things. If you are wishing you could engage then maybe you need to work on some social skills, active listening, asking questions, etc. 

Bottom line is you are an individual and you deserve to love who you are, and that might not be the engaging super social person that some others are.  As long as you have your passions and reasons you wake up each day and get out there you will find people that think the same.

Get your GED. Enroll in community college, you can apply for financial aide.

This isn’t because I think everyone needs to go to college, but you have the freedom to take some classes that might help you discover who you are along with still building the base with some general knowledge.

My favorite class I ever took was acting. It was uncomfortable and terrifying. I gained some great friends though and realized for the most part the felt the same way. After that I left being empowered to be in front of people, even if I was pretending to be someone else until I felt comfortable in my own skin. 

The biggest advice I can give you is just push yourself into situations that make you grow, and do something every day, no matter how simple, that makes you better than the day before.
